review_kind: read-only independent source/authority comparison; no model or new tests run
checks: Fixed64 uses 63 / (t64 - t1), includes natural EOS at event 64, and is null with fewer than 64 events.

The historical comparison drops terminal EOS and uses (N - 1) / (tN - t1), N=min(64, non-EOS events), null for N<2. The 28.49 reference has eleven nonzero prompt rates per repeat because code-review stopped immediately.
Submission100 uses 99 / (t100 - t1), first 100 generated events. EOS at event 100 has a valid window; earlier EOS yields null. The numerator is never 100.
The primary aggregate takes the conventional median within each prompt class, then the conventional median of those class medians; the all-prompt median is secondary.
The prompt-class mapping exactly matches scripts/qualify_realistic_window_metrics.py, including separate documentation and structured-writing classes.
Timestamp count equals emitted-token count. Timestamps must be finite, strictly increasing, and after request start. Event count, interval count, numerator and endpoints remain recorded.

Raw fields cover timestamps, TTFT, actual prompt/output counts, cached tokens zero, wall rate, early end, finish reason, requested cap, hashes and helper metadata. Integer top-level count medians match the helper.

Top-level statistics use repeat 1. Each repeat has a separate summary; pooled historical rates have a distinct name. The synthetic warmup excludes measured prompts and request reset precedes every measured request.
Caps 64/128, subsets and repeats cannot authorize submission: both final-gate markers remain false. Model/runtime identity, promotion attestation and the requested 512-token cap remain required.
limitations: Current caps are screening evidence, not a 512-cap final gate or submission-ready payload.
Partial or failed suites may report descriptive statistics for successful rows, explicitly labeled; these cannot pass the final gate.
TTFT and wall timestamp capture still require coordinator device receipt qualification.

The 28.49 external reference uses different arithmetic/runtime/KV/context and excludes an immediate-EOG prompt from its rate median. Current oracle populations differ; formula parity alone does not imply matched quality or benchmark identity.
